$comment: Accepted trigger names, and the alternate spellings that must keep working. This exists because models/communication.model.ts and enhanced-event-handler.ts DISAGREE: the enum declares APPOINTMENT_RESCHEDULED while the switch matches APPOINTMENT_RESCHEDULING, and eight handled event types are not enum members at all. Both spellings are in production callers, so both resolve to the same playbook. The engine's own trigger type is a plain string — it does not enumerate what events exist, which is exactly how the enum and the switch came to drift apart unnoticed.
known: $comment: seeded from the service modules rather than the switch
$comment.APPOINTMENT_MISSED: Declared, but NO playbook handles it. It is in the source's EventType enum and its EHR mapper maps appointment_no_show / appointment_missed onto it, and then the 17-case switch has no case for it and drops it with a logger.warn (D56). So the EHR path for a missed appointment has always been a no-op. Declaring it keeps ehr-mapping.json coherent and turns the drop into a SKIPPED playbook_runs row instead of silence. Authoring the playbook is new capability, not a port (D59) — a tenant's call.
